entry.title: Creating a good online presence: what is the best approach?
Custom Domains for Next.js: The Cloudflare + Vercel Setup That Works in 2026
entry.summary:
You shipped a Next.js app to Vercel. It's live at your-project-xxx.vercel.app\. Everything works, but the URL looks like a throwaway demo. Getting a real domain is a 30-minute task, but it's easy to make mistakes that cost you SSL certificates, SEO, or deliverability. Here's the exact flow I used to move my template business from a vercel.app URL to my own domain. Production-tested, 2026-current. Registrar: Cloudflare Registrar (at-cost pricing) DNS: Cloudflare DNS (free, fastest propagation) Hosting: Vercel Email Routing: Cloudflare Email Routing (free receiving) Email Sending: Loops.so Zero monthly cost except the domain itself (~$12/year for .dev). Use Cloudflare Registrar, not Namecheap or GoDaddy. Prices are wholesale, WHOIS privacy is free, and DNS is managed in the same dashboard. dash.cloudflare.com → Domain Registration → Register Domain Search your domain 2 years with auto-renew ON Pay. Domain is yours in ~60 seconds Open your Vercel project → Settings → Domains
Click Add Domain
Enter your domain Uncheck "Redirect to www" — apex as canonical is cleaner in 2026 Save Vercel shows Invalid Configuration. Expected. Click Edit in Vercel → Manual setup. Vercel shows: \ \ Vercel is migrating from the old A record (76.76.21.21) to CNAME-based records. Cloudflare → your domain → DNS → Records → Add record: \ \ Why DNS only matters: Cloudflare proxy ON intercepts HTTPS, so Vercel can't issue SSL. Keep it gray. Vercel auto-detects propagation in 2-10 minutes. Green check = done. DNS spec (RFC 1912) doesn't allow CNAMEs on apex. Cloudflare solves this with CNAME Flattening — internally resolves to IP, returns A record. You don't do anything special. AWS Route 53 calls this "ALIAS". Google Cloud DNS has similar. If your DNS provider doesn't support this, use A record with Vercel's IP instead. \\ Originally published on Craftly. Car traffic plummeted as people sheltered at home and shifted to remote work. Air travel collapsed. Introducing Blazar: Quicknode's Purpose-Built Solana WebSocket Solution
entry.summary: Solana's native WebSocket PubSub drops messages under load and leaves three subscription methods unstable. Blazar fixes that at the infrastructure level, with sub-millisecond overhead, full method support, and no SDK changes required.
